title: Focus returns to the opener and moves on when a focused card leaves
custom_preconds:
• Owner/Admin with Work Orders View and Create & Edit permissions; browser at least 1024 px wide. Two active, clockable technicians A and B are eligible at the location.
  • Two Approved work orders for one unique customer are led by A. Use technicians without active work-order shifts so reassignment does not require a clock-out prompt.
  • Open Work Orders → All → Board View, search for the customer and clear other filters; Assigned to me off. Mouse use is allowed for setup and applying the Technician filter.
  • Keyboard navigation: Tab enters the board at the last-focused card, or first card if none. Use arrow keys between cards/headers and Tab to reach the focused item’s controls.

Source: PRD v60, S11-R1, S11-R3, S11-R5, S11-R6, S11-E1 and S1-R15.

Execution dependency: The Technician filter must be available. The latest execution is blocked by SV-11326 (Open, checked 16 Oct 2026). Rerun when available; automation remains on hold pending execution.
custom_steps:
1. Use the keyboard to focus the first card in A’s column, then Tab to its More actions button.
  2. Press Enter to open More actions, then Esc.
  3. Open More actions again, choose reassignment with the keyboard, then press Esc to cancel the dialog.
  4. Apply Technician = A. Return keyboard focus to the first card in A’s column.
  5. Use More actions to reassign that work order to B with the keyboard.
  6. Use the keyboard to reassign A’s remaining work order to B.
  7. Continue navigating with the keyboard from the focused header.
custom_expected:
Step 1: A visible focus indicator identifies the card and then its More actions button.

Step 2: The menu closes without changes and focus returns to its opening button.

Step 3: The dialog closes without reassignment and focus returns to the control that opened it.

Step 4: Only A’s column is shown, containing both work orders; the first card has visible keyboard focus.

Step 5: The reassigned card leaves the filtered results. Focus moves to the next card in A’s column and stays visible.

Step 6: The last card leaves the filtered results. Nothing matches the filters any more, so the board shows “No work orders match these filters”, and keyboard focus moves to its Clear all filters button and stays visible. PRD version 70 (20 Oct 2026), S11-E1: “When the move leaves nothing matching the filters, so the board or table is replaced by the “No work orders match these filters” empty state (S1-N1a), for example moving the last work order of the only technician chosen in the Technician filter, focus moves to its Clear all filters button.”

Step 7: Keyboard navigation continues normally from the header; focus is visible and is not lost or trapped.
